changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/10864-app-shell-spec-floor.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` — edited by this change

  > `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` imports `predicateSlotRefusal` from `@objectstack/spec/automation`; `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/simulator/flow-sim-validate.ts` imports `structuralConditionRefusal` from the same subpath plus `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED` and `EvaluatedExpressionSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/shared`. `@objectstack/spec` was declared as `^17.3.0`, so any resolution landing on 17.3.0 (which the range allows) gets a module that names exports its own declared spec dependency does not have.

### `.changeset/5920-flow-runner-translation-overlay.md`

- names `screen-spec.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` — edited by this change

  > ⚠️ **Dated note, 2026-09-28 — the declared floor has since moved again — objectui#10864.** At this change `@object-ui/app-shell` declared `^17.3.0`, and the paragraph above is kept as the reading of that change: `17.3.0` was in fact the first release exporting the resolver family this fix uses. Later in this same release the floor was raised again, to `^17.4.0`, because two other shipped app-shell sources (`screen-spec.ts`, `flow-sim-validate.ts`) import four symbols (`predicateSlotRefusal`, `structuralConditionRefusal`, `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED`, `EvaluatedExpressionSchema`) that `17.3.0` does not export — a defect this changeset's own range did not introduce and did not need to guard against. `@object-ui/app-shell` now declares `^17.4.0`.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `e978ed5ea` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1794 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2401 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36691454349)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7d9c24c282675af3c35b0a06f71dd5b8d745b280`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #9248 (body and its five comments: unlock `5852969116`, unlock `5904174295`, claim `5906696061`, dev report `5907589570`, claim amendment `5907646725`); PR #11188 (body, the 7-file list, the net diff against `main`); the 43 check-runs on the head read with `filter=latest`: 40 success, 3 skipped, 0 failed, 0 in progress at judgment (the eight test shards, `Spec Main Shape Gate` and the `Test` aggregate all completed while this review waited). Context reads at the head and at objectstack `0f6dcac5e9` went through `contents`; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. The four keys read straight off the installed 17.5.0 `ScreenFieldSpec`, no widened local copy — RIGHT. `ScreenView.tsx` still re-exports `ScreenFieldSpec` verbatim from `@objectstack/spec/contracts` (that hunk is untouched) and the diff reads `field.min` / `field.max` / `field.inlineHelpText` / `field.reference` on that type; the contract at `0f6dcac5e9` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`) declares exactly those four, all optional. The local `ScreenSpec` alias (only `fields` widened) is unchanged. No alias and no screen-local vocabulary. `help` / `helpText` / `hint` / `tooltip` occur once, in a header comment naming them as spec refusals, and are read nowhere; `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` maps them onto `inlineHelpText` in the `aliases` table of a strict object, so they are refusals carrying a rename prescription, as the dev's premise 1 says.
2. Native `min` / `max` on the numeric input — RIGHT. Written only when `htmlType === 'number'` (`number` and `currency`); a `date` or text input receives `undefined`, so the attribute is omitted. Pinned, including a lone `min: 0`.
3. `screenFieldBoundViolations` against the engine — RIGHT, parity read on `validateScreenInputs` in `packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts` at `0f6dcac5e9`. The engine's bound pass skips unless `typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value)`, refuses a value below `min` or above `max` (the limits themselves pass), skips a `visibleWhen` field whose visibility probe is not `true`, and leaves an absent value to `required`. The helper applies the same four clauses over `visibleScreenFields`, and a pin covers each. One nuance, pre-existing and not introduced here: the engine treats an UNEVALUABLE predicate as hidden while the client's `visibleScreenFields` fails open (renders, so compares) — the same split `required` already has at base, and it follows the card's "same on-screen list" rule. The engine's separate `invalid_type` pass on `type: 'number'` needs no client twin: the numeric input emits `Number(...)` or `undefined`, never a string.
4. `inlineHelpText` below the control, named in `aria-describedby` — RIGHT. Drawn as its own paragraph element after the control (document order pinned) with id `ff-NAME-help`, and `describedBy` is threaded to the Input, the Textarea, the Checkbox, the SelectTrigger and the lookup widget. Pinned as the accessible description on the text, number, textarea, boolean and select arms. The lookup arm receives the prop through the same `toDomProps` spread that carries its pinned `aria-required`, but has no description pin of its own — noted, not a defect.
5. The lookup — RIGHT. `getLazyFieldWidget('lookup')` returns the cached `React.lazy` loader of `LookupField` from the static loader map in `@object-ui/fields`, the seam `ActionParamDialog` reads; it is resolved once at module scope, after the registry module has evaluated, and rendered behind its own Suspense boundary because `ScreenPreview` renders `ScreenView` with none. `dataSource` is passed as the explicit prop, which `LookupField` ranks first (explicit prop, then the field, then `SchemaRendererContext`), fed from `ScreenView`'s existing `dataSource` prop; `LookupField` reads `field.reference` as its target object. Pinned with no `SchemaRendererProvider`, through `ScreenView`, through `FlowRunner`'s host `dataSource`, and in the Studio preview, each asserting the queried object NAME.
6. A lookup with no `reference` keeps a text input — RIGHT, and the brief's question is answered by the spec itself: the `ScreenFieldSpec.reference` doc on the wire contract says the key stays optional there because the shape also describes a `ScreenSpec` rehydrated from a run suspended before the key existed, and that a client meeting one "falls back to a plain input — the pre-#17306 behaviour, kept reachable on purpose rather than turned into a client-side crash". The REQUIRED-when-`lookup` rule lives on the authoring side (`ScreenFieldConfigSchema`'s `superRefine`, refusing on path `reference`), so a parsed flow never reaches the client without it. The fallback is the contract's prescription, not a local choice.
7. The ratified `screen-spec.ts` projection carry — RIGHT. `toScreenFields` carries the four keys typeof-guarded to the spec's declared types (number, number, string, string); a half-typed row adds nothing (pinned). Ratified at `5907646725`; the file is on the PR's list.
8. The byte-identical key-less control — RIGHT on the code read. With no key present, `helpId` is `undefined` so no help element renders, `aria-describedby` / `min` / `max` are `undefined` and omitted, and the lookup branch is not entered; a `type: 'lookup'` field WITHOUT `reference` keeps the text Input it always had. The CONTROL pins (two children per field block, no `-help` id, no lookup trigger, no bounds, no `aria-describedby`) run in the green shards; the dev's byte-for-byte `cmp` (21501 bytes at HEAD and at BASE) is its own local run and is consistent with the read.
9. The 24 pins and the 5 ablation legs — CONSISTENT. 14 in `ScreenView.boundHelpReference-9248.test.tsx`, 7 in `__tests__/FlowRunner.bounds-9248.test.tsx`, 3 in `previews/ScreenPreview.boundHelpReference-9248.test.tsx`; all three files are in the test program CI ran. The reported red counts (4 / 2 / 4 / 3 / 3) match which pins assert each mutated site; the legs are the dev's local runs and are not re-derived here.
10. i18n — RIGHT. `validation.min`, `validation.max` and `validation.formInvalidJoiner` exist in `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` with the `{{field}}` / `{{min}}` / `{{max}}` holes the runner fills; no key is added; `check:i18n-keys` and `Lint` are green.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/9248-screen-field-bound-help-reference.md`, `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` — ACCEPTED. What the diff publishes is behaviour on an existing surface. `@object-ui/app-shell`'s index exports `FlowRunner` and the types `FlowRunnerProps` / `ScreenFlowState` / `ScreenSpec` / `ScreenFieldSpec` (the last two being the spec's re-exports, unchanged); `ScreenView`, `ScreenFieldInput`, the new `screenFieldBoundViolations` and `ScreenFieldBoundViolation` are not on the package index and the package's `exports` map is the root entry only, so the new helper widens no public surface, and `FlowRunnerProps` is untouched. `Clause-②: no` is on the PR body and is RIGHT: no objectui-owned accept set or public surface moves; the accept set is the spec's. The `feat` title with a `patch` bump is the weaker of two legitimate readings (among the pending changesets 35 `feat(` entries declare `minor` and 4 declare `patch`; no rule binds the pair, the fixed group versions together, and the body frames the change as declared-but-inert keys made to render). `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Claim Re-read` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviations named in dev report `5907589570`:
- The widening to `metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` — ANSWERED: ratified by claim amendment `5907646725`. The projection dropped the keys at base (premise 5 falsified), the carry is typeof-guarded, and the `preview-projection` leg with the three preview pins is its evidence.
- `git fetch origin main` in the shared `/home/user/objectstack` checkout — ANSWERED as a process deviation, not a contract defect. No file was edited and no branch moved, but it advanced the shared `origin/main` (`41dcf1188` to `df67985b0`) and the common-dir `FETCH_HEAD`, the exact hazard the multi-agent rules list for anyone restoring from a moving ref in that checkout. A safe spelling existed (a `contents/...?ref=main` read, or a fetch into a self-named ref). Declared, bounded, and of no effect on this diff; the seat should re-derive any `origin/main`-relative reading it made in that checkout during that window.
- The lookup reuse — ANSWERED: not a deviation; it is the seam the dispatch named.

`open_questions`: none declared. The brief's own question (the fallback for a `lookup` without `reference`) is answered in ① item 6.

Out-of-scope findings:
- The Studio preview also drops `options` / `placeholder` / `defaultValue` — CONFIRMED and ESCALATED to the seat. The named producer exists at `0f6dcac5e9`: `examples/app-todo/src/flows/task.flow.ts`, screen node `screen_1`, field `priority` (`select` with `options` and `defaultValue: 'normal'`) and field `category` (`select` with `options`). The gap predates this PR (the base projection already dropped them) and `defaultValue` carries the engine's suspend-time interpolation, so it is a separate card, which the amendment says the seat handles at accept.
- `inlineHelpText` is untranslated — ANSWERED: `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_COPY_KEYS` is the spec's face and lists `label` and `placeholder`; `overlayFieldCopy` walks that constant, so the runner follows the day the spec lists the key, and the runner header's "deliberately not localized" list now names it. Nothing to do in objectui; the carrier is a spec-side widening in objectstack, for the seat to file if it wants one.
- The flow designer's screen-field editor was not measured — ANSWERED: an authoring surface outside this rendering card. Note that `check:designer-field-key-parity` (green) gates the EMIT side only, keys a designer writes that the spec refuses; its header says under-coverage stays a separate card, so its green says nothing about whether the editor offers the four keys.
